messages.author: 3b16cd5074875dd7
messages.subject: pystan does not support user specified initial parameter values/bug in misc.py?
parts:
Hi - does pystan support user-specified initial parameter values right now?  

I am looking at the end of the _get_valid_stan_args function in misc.py (on the develop branch).  I'm a bit confused, because unless init is a string_types or a Sequence, init is set to 'random'.  But this function is setting the arguments for each chain.  In the call to pystan.stan, init could have been a list of dictionaries, and one element from that list(a dictionary) is passed to _get_valid_stan_args.  But now even if that one element of the list is a dictionary, args['init'] is still set to 'random'.

I tried changing line 558 of misc.py to:
      elif isinstance(init, dict)

But then I got an error saying that a parameter is not specified.

So another question I have is: what should the format of the args['init_list'] in line 560 of misc.py be, if we want to specify the initial parameter values?

Thanks,
-Fulton

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] pystan does not support user specified initial parameter values/bug in misc.py?
parts:
The way this is done in command-line Stan is to allow:

1. "init=<number>" --- inits between [-num,+num] on the unconstrained scale

2. "init=<file>" : Read inits from file

But command-line Stan doesn't deal with multiple chains.
RStan follows R2WinBUGS and R2jags in allowing the above, plus:

3. "init=<list<list>>" : list of lists of values, one per chain

4. "init=<fun>" : function mapping chain id to list of values

It'd be great to support all of these options in PyStan.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: pystan does not support user specified initial parameter values/bug in misc.py?
parts:
Hello,

I wanted to inquire about the status of initial parameter specification with pystan.  

I'm checking because I have found that I get an "INDEX OPERATOR" error (below) when I specify initial parameters.  Many of the parameters in my model (including the flagged raw_t1.) are 2 dimensional, with the first dimension tagging the object ID and the second dimension equaling 5 (the number of type options for the data).  The error only happens when I specify initial parameters and try to fit the model with more than 1 object, i.e. the parameter shape specified to be [>1,5] (one object, or [1,5], works fine).  Fitting the model with more than 1 object works fine with random initial parameters.

Note that I don't think this problem is due to incorrect dimensions in the initial parameter specification.  If I introduce a problem of that type, I get a different error ("mismatch in number dimensions declared and found in context").

Any suggestions for how to debug or fix this problem are welcome, and my thanks to the PyStan team!

Best,

~Nathan


----------

    318                      sample_file=sample_file, diagnostic_file=diagnostic_file,
--> 319                      verbose=verbose, algorithm=algorithm, control=control, **kwargs)

    650         else:
--> 651             ret_and_samples = [call_sampler_star(a) for a in call_sampler_args]
    652         samples = [smpl for _, smpl in ret_and_samples]
    653 

/tmp/tmpyzNGmH/pystan/stanfit4anon_model_219d0c842cca67098c13d55b374b50ab.so in stanfit4anon_model_219d0c842cca67098c13d55b374b50ab._call_sampler_star (/tmp/tmpyzNGmH/pystan/stanfit4anon_model_219d0c842cca67098c13d55b374b50ab.cpp:4102)()

IndexError: INDEX OPERATOR [] OUT OF BOUNDS; index=6; lower bound=1; upper bound=5; index position=2; raw_t1

On Sunday, November 17, 2013 2:36:48 PM UTC-5, Fulton Wang wrote:
Hi - does pystan support user-specified initial parameter values right now?  

I am looking at the end of the _get_valid_stan_args function in misc.py (on the develop branch).  I'm a bit confused, because unless init is a string_types or a Sequence, init is set to 'random'.  But this function is setting the arguments for each chain.  In the call to pystan.stan, init could have been a list of dictionaries, and one element from that list(a dictionary) is passed to _get_valid_stan_args.  But now even if that one element of the list is a dictionary, args['init'] is still set to 'random'.

I tried changing line 558 of misc.py to:
      elif isinstance(init, dict)

But then I got an error saying that a parameter is not specified.

So another question I have is: what should the format of the args['init_list'] in line 560 of misc.py be, if we want to specify the initial parameter values?

Thanks,
-Fulton

parts:
Hi Allen,

While trying to put together a minimal working example for you, I'm glad to say I found the problem!  I had a typo in my prior specification where I was accidentally indexing both dimensions of the array with the object ID (k).  I mistakenly thought the model was working fine when I tested with k<=5, since the second dimension has length 5.

I've attached the MWE below if you want to see what I mean.

I should have seen this earlier given that the error specified the raw_t1 variable.  If there i some way to specify the line number in the model when this error is returned, it may help others with this problem.

Thanks, again!

Best,

~Nathan

----

## Model
stanmodel="""
data {
    int<lower=0> K;
}

parameters {
  real pt0[K];
  real raw_t1[K,5];
}

model {
    for (k in 1:K) {
raw_t1[k][k] ~ normal(0,1);
    }
}
"""

## Data
mydata={'K':7}

## Initialization function
def myinit():
    params={}
    params['pt0']=zeros(7)
    params['raw_t1']=zeros([7,5])
    return params

## Try sampling
fit = pystan.stan(model_code=stanmodel, data=mydata, iter=100, chains=1, init=myinit)

parts:
We've thought about how to push the line number
of the model through along with the actual call structure
(there's a function name but not the actual variables being
passed). I can't figure out how to do it without rewriting
our whole math lib at this point to pass the line-number
information from the Stan model to the C++ translation as
a string literal and then pass it through at run time so
it's availble when there's a problem.

Maybe there's a better way to do this that we haven't
thought about? Let us know if anyone has suggestions.

- Bob
